- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–7 day) horizons; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 1–3 day forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch momentum.
- For 15+ day forecasts, model often misses downward trend; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., -0.3+ to +0.3+ in 3 days), model fails to adjust; re-forecast with 1–2% correction toward sentiment direction.
